objective: Reassess available evidence across batches after new laboratory result LAB-0300.

report.assessment: New laboratory result LAB-0300 (available 2025-03-12T12:15:00Z) is an action-level upstream microbiological signal for in-progress BATCH-099: relative_bioburden_signal 1.71 action-limit ratio against an action limit of 1.0 (alert 0.7), status 'action', reported consistently in three laboratory exports (lims_export.csv, microbiology_results.xlsx, lims_review_local.csv at 171.0 % of limit). It is the third action-level upstream bioburden result on a LINE-A Famotidine Injection batch: BATCH-075 (LAB-0225, 1.23, 2024-12-01) and BATCH-084 (LAB-0255, 1.48, 2025-01-04) preceded it, and the source-reported values rise across the series. Both earlier batches were dispositioned 'released' and shipped while their high-severity microbiology deviations (DEV-0003, DEV-0005) remain open with no recorded root cause or CAPA. An independent environmental co-signal exists for BATCH-099: EM-0100 (process support area, gram-negative morphology, 1.09, status 'action') was sampled ten minutes after the batch sample; the equivalent environmental results for BATCH-075 (0.71) and BATCH-084 (0.86) were at alert level. No deviation record exists yet for BATCH-099 and no repeat, resample or invalidation record exists for LAB-0300, although the package contains a precedent (LAB-0043, SYN-0014) where an action-level repeat result was invalidated and a resample returned 0.22 (normal). Historian parameters for BATCH-099 are inside expected ranges with severity 'normal', and maintenance records contain only planned, closed inspections. What the evidence supports: a recurring, unresolved upstream microbiological control problem on LINE-A that has now reached its highest recorded level on a batch that is still in production, with an unconfirmed single reading and an unexplained environmental co-signal. What remains unknown: whether LAB-0300 reflects the batch state (no resample), the organism identity in the batch sample, the root cause of the prior two deviations, finished-product endotoxin/sterility outcomes for BATCH-099 (batch still in progress), and any product-impact assessment for the two released batches. All records in this package carry provenance 'synthetic_factory_signal' and the exports are labeled 'SYNTHETIC FACTORY RECORDS'; the investigation treats them as the available evidence. Retrieval budget was exhausted before deterministic metric receipts (calculate_metrics) or further row transcription could be produced, so no computed metrics are certified in this report and several lower-priority items remain explicitly unreviewed. Coverage status: of 417 screening units, 23 are unit-level investigated, 14 reviewed with per-entity retrieval, and 380 remain deferred or unresolved at unit level (population-level screening only) because the retrieval budget was exhausted; this is why the report is submitted as a partial investigation.

report.cross_scope_synthesis: Shared pattern: across laboratory, environmental, batch, quality, manufacturing and maintenance sources, the only material signals converge on one storyline - recurring action-level upstream microbiological results on LINE-A famotidine batches. The laboratory sources (lims_export.csv and its microbiology mirror, plus the local-timezone review export) agree exactly on four action-status results: LAB-0010/SYN-0004 (1.08, Feb 2024), LAB-0225/BATCH-075 (1.23, Dec 2024), LAB-0255/BATCH-084 (1.48, Jan 2025) and LAB-0300/BATCH-099 (1.71, Mar 2025). The environmental source adds a parallel series in the same 'process support area' location: EM-0075 0.71 (alert), EM-0085 0.86 (alert), EM-0100 1.09 (action, gram-negative morphology) - the environmental signal crosses the action threshold only for BATCH-099. The quality source shows each earlier real-batch signal generated an open high-severity microbiology deviation (DEV-0003, DEV-0005) with no root cause or CAPA, while the batch records show both batches were released and shipped; no deviation record exists yet for BATCH-099. Exceptions and counterevidence: the SYN-batch history contains an invalidated-repeat precedent (LAB-0043, SYN-0014: 1.06 invalidated, resample 0.22 normal) showing that a high reading can be a sampling or analytical error, and most SYN deviations were closed as isolated procedural variances, so recurrence is not uniform across the package; BATCH-099's historian events are all inside expected ranges with severity 'normal', and maintenance shows only planned, closed inspections, so no equipment-parameter excursion co-occurs in available data. The 1399 machine-screening flags are overwhelmingly clock-quality artifacts (missing_source_time) on single-event records - limit, expected-range and result cells that carry calendar timestamps but no elapsed process clock - and must not be read as process anomalies; all 12 priority candidates are of this type, and the one with material content is the LAB-0300 review-export row. Missing evidence that limits synthesis: no resample or repeat for LAB-0300, no organism identification for the batch sample, no endotoxin/sterility results for BATCH-099 yet, no root-cause or CAPA content for the two open deviations, no sanitation or environmental control records, no recipe/controller/calibration data, an unreadable package_manifest.json, untranscribed lims_review_local row 111 and process_event_points pages beyond page 1. All records carry 'synthetic_factory_signal' provenance and the package is labeled 'SYNTHETIC FACTORY RECORDS', so conclusions apply to this evidence package as provided. No child investigations were completed because the shared retrieval budget was exhausted during lead exploration; deterministic metric receipts could not be produced, so source-reported values are cited without computed comparisons.
